knowledge:
- key_parameters: testCovariate=The column name in pData representing the condition to test ;; cutoff=The coefficient threshold (magnitude of difference) for candidate region selection ;; adjustCovariate=Column name in pData to include directly in the model for adjustment ;; matchCovariate=Column name in pData to restrict permutations to balanced groups ;; block=Set to TRUE to detect large-scale methylation blocks ;; blockSize=Minimum basepairs for a candidate region to be considered a block (default 5000) ;; minInSpan=Minimum number of CpGs in a smoothing span (increase for blocks, e.g., 500) ;; bpSpan=Span in basepairs for smoothing (increase for blocks, e.g., 5e4) ;; maxGapSmooth=Maximum gap in basepairs allowed before smoothing is split (increase for blocks, e.g., 1e6) ;; maxGap=Maximum gap in basepairs between CpGs to allow merging into a single block (increase for blocks, e.g., 5e3)
- alternatives: bsseq (specifically BSmooth() which smooths each sample independently, whereas dmrseq smooths methylation differences once; do not use BSmooth() prior to dmrseq) ;; Bismark (upstream alignment tool to generate coverage/methylation counts)
- when_to_use: When scanning the genome to detect and perform statistical inference on differentially methylated regions (DMRs) or large-scale methylation blocks from Whole Genome Bisulfite Sequencing (WGBS) count data with at least 2 samples per condition.
- pitfalls: Do not use methylation proportions (M/Cov) directly as input because it discards coverage confidence information ;; Do not use bsseq's BSmooth() function prior to running dmrseq, as dmrseq smooths differences in a single step ;; At least 2 samples per condition are required to distinguish biological variability from inter-individual variability ;; Filter out CpGs with zero coverage across all samples in a group and remove extraneous samples before running dmrseq ;; Large-scale block detection can be computationally intensive and may fail to find enough null candidates for inference if run on too small a subset of data.

workflows.name: dmr_detection
workflows.intent: Scan the genome to detect and perform inference on local differentially methylated regions (DMRs) from WGBS count data.
input: sample_bismark.cov.gz (Bismark coverage files containing methylated and total read counts)
sample_metadata.csv (CSV file containing sample names and condition covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Load Bismark coverage files into a BSseq object using read.bismark ;; 2. Add sample metadata to the pData slot of the BSseq object ;; 3. Filter out CpGs with zero coverage and subset samples ;; 4. Run dmrseq to detect candidate regions and perform permutation-based inference ;; 5. Extract significant regions and calculate raw mean differences using meanDiff ;; 6. Visualize DMRs and empirical distributions using plotDMRs and plotEmpiricalDistribution
workflows.code:
library(dmrseq)
infile <- system.file("extdata/test_data.fastq_bismark.bismark.cov.gz",
                        package = 'bsseq')
bismarkBSseq <- read.bismark(files = infile,
                               rmZeroCov = TRUE,
                               strandCollapse = FALSE,
                               verbose = TRUE)
bismarkBSseq

bs <- BSseq(chr = chr, pos = pos,
            M = M, Cov = Cov, 
            sampleNames = sampleNames)
show(bs)

pData(bs)$CellType <- celltype
pData(bs)$Replicate <- substr(sampleNames, 
                              nchar(sampleNames), nchar(sampleNames))

pData(bs)

loci.idx <- which(DelayedMatrixStats::rowSums2(getCoverage(bs, type="Cov")==0) == 0)
sample.idx <- which(pData(bs)$CellType %in% c("imr90", "h1"))

bs.filtered <- bs[loci.idx, sample.idx]

testCovariate <- "CellType"
regions <- dmrseq(bs=bs[240001:260000,],
                  cutoff = 0.05,
                  testCovariate=testCovariate)
show(regions)

sum(regions$qval < 0.05)

sigRegions <- regions[regions$qval < 0.05,]

sum(sigRegions$stat > 0) / length(sigRegions)

annoTrack <- getAnnot("hg18")

plotDMRs(bs, regions=regions[1,], testCovariate="CellType",
    annoTrack=annoTrack)

plotEmpiricalDistribution(bs, testCovariate="CellType")

plotEmpiricalDistribution(bs, testCovariate="CellType", 
                          type="Cov", bySample=TRUE)

rawDiff <- meanDiff(bs, dmrs=sigRegions, testCovariate="CellType")
str(rawDiff)

workflows.name: block_detection
workflows.intent: Detect large-scale, lower-resolution methylation blocks across the genome by adjusting smoothing and gap parameters.
input: sample_metadata.csv (CSV file containing sample names and condition covariates)
bs_object.rds (Pre-constructed BSseq object containing WGBS count data)
workflows.stages: 1. Run dmrseq with block = TRUE and increased smoothing parameters (minInSpan, bpSpan, maxGapSmooth, maxGap) ;; 2. Visualize the detected blocks using plotDMRs
workflows.code:
testCovariate <- "CellType"
blocks <- dmrseq(bs=bs[120001:125000,],
                  cutoff = 0.05,
                  testCovariate=testCovariate,
                  block = TRUE,
                  minInSpan = 500,
                  bpSpan = 5e4,
                  maxGapSmooth = 1e6,
                  maxGap = 5e3)
head(blocks)

plotDMRs(bs, regions=blocks[1,], testCovariate="CellType",
    annoTrack=annoTrack)

workflows.name: dmr_simulation
workflows.intent: Split samples from the same condition into artificial groups and spike in in silico DMRs to assess the sensitivity and specificity of DMR detection.
input: bs_object.rds (Pre-constructed BSseq object containing WGBS count data from multiple samples of the same biological condition)
workflows.stages: 1. Reorder or subset samples to create a null comparison ;; 2. Run simDMRs to generate a simulated BSseq object with spiked-in DMRs ;; 3. Retrieve coordinates and effect sizes of the simulated DMRs
workflows.code:
data(BS.chr21)

# reorder samples to create a null comparison 
BS.null <- BS.chr21[1:20000,c(1,3,2,4)]

# add 100 DMRs
BS.chr21.sim <- simDMRs(bs=BS.null, num.dmrs=100)

# bsseq object with original null + simulated DMRs
show(BS.chr21.sim$bs)

# coordinates of spiked-in DMRs
show(BS.chr21.sim$gr.dmrs)

# effect sizes
head(BS.chr21.sim$delta)
